newsitem.title: MEXICO: NYSE approves listing of two Mexican companies.
newsitem.headline: NYSE approves listing of two Mexican companies.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) has approved the listing of two Mexican companies before the end of this year, although there is no firm date, officials said here Thursday.
"We currently have approved two Mexican companies before the end of the year," Georges Ugeux, international vice-president of the NYSE, told a news conference.
He declined to name the companies, and said that though approval had been given, there was no guarantee the listings would take place.

Some 22 Mexican companies currently trade on the NYSE and exchange chairman Richard Grasso said about 50 more Mexican firms met the high standards required for issuing American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Grasso is in Mexico seeking to drum up interest in the exchange in which the most active issue for the last two years has been Mexican telephone giant Telefonos de Mexico.

He said the requirement that companies follow U.S. accounting standards had put off many potential issuers, but he said the Securities and Exchange Commission was making it easier for foreign companies to win approval to list on the NYSE.
